result.title: Unimodal Shortcuts and Joint Scene-Intent Dependence in Vision-Language Safety Representations
result.comment: 39 pages, 8 figures, 18 tables (14 pages main paper, 25 pages supplementary material)
result.summary: The safety of a request to a vision-language model often depends on the image: asking how to serve a dish is harmless for fresh food and harmful for spoiled food. High accuracy on situational safety benchmarks does not tell us whether a model's safety representation encodes both the scene and the user's intent, because a benchmark can often be solved from one modality alone. Studying frozen vision-language safety representations, we audit five public situational benchmarks and find that each admits a unimodal shortcut: images alone predict the labels, and on same-image prompt pairs a probe that never sees the photograph reaches 0.9645 AUROC. We therefore build a controlled evaluation that crosses safe and hazardous scenes with observation and action requests, so that no single-modality rule can exceed 0.500 group-ranking accuracy. On this control, linear probes on intermediate states of Qwen3-VL-8B and SmolVLM2-2.2B reach 0.958 and 0.930, showing that the scene-intent conjunction is linearly decodable; concatenating separately encoded image and text states already recovers most of this signal, so decodability is not evidence of a fusion mechanism. The same probes screen cheaply but generalize poorly to unseen images and other benchmarks. Reliable multimodal safety evaluation therefore needs controls that rule out unimodal shortcuts before accuracy is read as evidence of joint understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 该文审计五个情境安全基准中的单模态捷径，并构造交叉场景与意图的受控评估，用线性探针检验 Qwen3-VL 与 SmolVLM2 中间状态是否线性编码场景—意图联合信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 它直接诊断 VLM 内部状态中是保留视觉证据还是依赖文本捷径，并指出拼接单模态表征即可恢复大部分信号、探针可解码不等于融合机制，可供核查 latent 表示的内容保留、视觉旁路与探针评价效度。
